summary: Backend-only testing of the new permission system (leader/member roles + edit_scales/edit_songs/edit_announcements). Created /app/backend/tests/test_permissions.py with 24 tests mapping 1:1 to every bullet of the review_request: signup creates leader with all 3 perms via to_public_user, signup-with-invite-code creates member with permissions=[], /auth/me exposes permissions, all forbidden write ops (POST/PUT/DELETE) for members without perms return 403, members granted a single perm succeed on that op only, announcement author can delete own without edit_announcements, non-author without perm gets 403, members (even with all perms) can't PUT /ministry/members/{id} nor rotate api-key (403), leader can promote/demote, set permissions, invalid perm name -> 400, last-leader self-demote -> 400 'precisa de ao menos um líder', self-demote allowed when another leader exists, promoted member exposes all 3 perms via to_public_user. Re-ran existing test_louvorapp_backend.py + test_external_api.py as regression. Result: 24/24 new + 48/48 regression = 72/72 passing.
action_items: Frontend (out of scope but observed): Metro bundler currently FAILS to bundle app/(tabs)/index.tsx with 'SyntaxError: Unexpected token (339:2)'. A stray '8,' is sitting between StyleSheet objects (lines 337-339). This must be fixed before any frontend can be reached, but does NOT affect backend permission system which is fully functional.
critical_code_review_comments: to_public_user correctly always returns ALL_PERMS for leaders regardless of stored permissions array (line 185), so promoted members instantly gain full perms - verified.

PUT /ministry/members/{member_id} correctly scopes the lookup to the caller's ministry_id (line 336), preserving multi-tenant isolation - a leader of ministry A cannot touch a member of ministry B (would 404).
Last-leader protection at lines 343-349 correctly counts other leaders with $ne member_id, allowing safe self-demote only when another leader exists.
Suggestion (non-blocking): require_leader/require_perm could be FastAPI Depends-style dependencies (DRY) instead of inline calls inside each endpoint - works either way.
Suggestion (non-blocking): UpdateMemberReq has no validator for empty body; lines 357-358 already raise 400 'Nada para atualizar' so behavior is correct.
Suggestion (non-blocking): consider an audit log for role/permission changes; currently no trace of who promoted whom.
Note: PERM constants and ALL_PERMS set used consistently; validation against ALL_PERMS at line 352 is correct.
